Run the three “Next Commands” in order; they’re already the right next step given you have a current champion and no PASS/INCONCLUSIVE candidates.

## 1) Run AUB autopilot (module-level search, pick best)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
What to look for afterward:
- A new candidate promoted/selected as “best” vs `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`
- Whether it improves **tuning_mean/min** and/or **lockbox_mean/min** (and doesn’t regress one badly while slightly improving the other)
- Any failures/flaky eval notes (if present)

## 2) Run system autopilot (system candidate sweep)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
What to look for:
- Whether any system-level candidates beat the champion on your primary metric(s)
- Any clear tradeoffs (e.g., better tuning but worse lockbox)

## 3) Generate the “next fix” report (actionable changes)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
This should produce a prioritized set of fixes to try next (often based on where evals are failing/regressing).

---

If you paste the console output (or the resulting report paths / summary tables), I can help:
- decide whether to accept a new champion,
- identify regressions vs. your current champion numbers,
- and propose the next candidate(s) to try.
